$comment: Declarative tool list for Setup-Workstation.ps1. Edit this file to add,
remove, retier or disable a tool - no PowerShell changes needed.
This covers the ANALYST WORKSTATION tier. The KAPE parsing toolchain
(EZ Tools CLI, Hayabusa, Chainsaw, Hindsight, RegRipper, NirSoft) is NOT
here: those are tightly coupled to KAPE's own module layout and live in
Manage-Tools.ps1, which knows each one's quirks (Chainsaw's sigma
submodule, RegRipper's plugin tree, where KAPE expects each binary).
FIELDS
Name        Display name; also what -Include/-Exclude match on.
Tier        Standard = installed by default.
Optional = only with -Tier Optional or -Include <name>.
Enabled     false hides it entirely until you flip it.
Why         Free text - kept in the manifest so a future reader knows
why this tool was on the box.
Source.Type GitHubRelease | Url | PSModule
Source.Repo owner/repo, for GitHubRelease.
Source.AssetPattern  regex matched against release asset names. Must
select exactly one Windows x64 asset.
Source.Url  direct download, for Url type. May contain {version}.
Install.Type  Zip | Msi | Exe | PSModule
Install.Dest  folder under -ToolsRoot (Zip/Exe) - ignored for Msi,
which installs wherever the package decides.
Install.Flatten  true unwraps a single top-level folder in the zip.
Verify.Path   path under -ToolsRoot proving the install worked; for Msi
use Verify.Registry instead (an uninstall DisplayName match).
Adding a tool is usually just: copy the nearest entry, change Repo and
AssetPattern. Run Setup-Workstation.ps1 -WhatIf to see what would resolve
without downloading anything (-DryRun, not -WhatIf).
Source.Type PSModule installs from the PowerShell Gallery instead of
downloading a file; Source.Module is the module name. Verify.Module
checks it is importable afterwards.

tools.Name: ImportExcel
tools.Why: Lets New-ReviewWorkbook.ps1 build the merged review workbook WITHOUT Microsoft Excel. A cloud investigation host has no Office install, so without this the workbook step degrades to a folder of CSVs - which is the tab-switching problem the workbook exists to solve.

tools.Name: Sysinternals
tools.Why: Autoruns, Procmon, Sigcheck, Strings - baseline live-triage and binary inspection.

tools.Name: Autopsy
tools.Why: Full GUI forensic suite for deeper work than KAPE triage output supports.

tools.Name: ripgrep
tools.Why: Fast recursive search across a multi-GB collection and across parsed CSV output. Single binary.

tools.Name: jq
tools.Why: Velociraptor emits JSON everywhere - client_info.json, uploads.json, artifact results. Single binary.

tools.Name: CAPA
tools.Why: Identifies what a suspicious PE actually does, offline. Pairs with the dropper paths collected by malware-drop-locations.csv.

tools.Name: DB Browser for SQLite
tools.Why: SQLite artifacts Hindsight does not parse - Teams, Slack, Signal, arbitrary app caches.

tools.Name: Loki
tools.Why: IOC and YARA-based scanner. Disabled by default: overlaps Hayabusa/Chainsaw detection and is heavy. Also the most practical way to get a YARA engine on the box, since VirusTotal ships YARA as source only - it has no official Windows release binary.

tools.Name: Notepad++
tools.Why: Large-log viewing. Disabled by default - taste, not capability.

tools.Name: LibreOffice
tools.Why: Opens the review workbook, and - more usefully - opens Office documents recovered FROM a collection, which nothing else on this host does. Disabled by default for two reasons: Timeline Explorer (already installed with the EZ Tools GUI suite) reads xlsx and is purpose-built for this review workflow, and a full office suite is a large document-parsing attack surface on a machine that handles attacker artifacts. If you enable it, set macro security to Very High before opening anything from a collection - see README.md.
tools.$versionNote: Pinned deliberately rather than resolved to 'latest': a forensic workstation benefits from a known, reproducible tool version, and the manifest records which one parsed a document. Bump this URL to move versions - listings are at https://download.documentfoundation.org/libreoffice/stable/
